target.effect_scale: OLS elasticity: log cumulative cases regressed on log annual exceedance days and log population density

substitutions.published: 55 randomly selected provincial-capital cities (identities not reported)
substitutions.reanalysis: All 107 official reporting provinces initially eligible; 100 entered the complete-case model
substitutions.reason: The article does not identify its random 55-city sample; public outcome data are provincial.

substitutions.reanalysis: Official cumulative confirmed cases reported by province
substitutions.reason: The publicly available national series is province-level; city-specific case totals were not supplied.

substitutions.published: Legambiente-derived regulatory-monitor total days exceeding PM10 or ozone limits in 2018
substitutions.reanalysis: CAMS reanalysis hourly PM10 and ozone at provincial-capital coordinates, aggregated using stated EU thresholds
substitutions.reason: Required independent public exposure source; avoids article-author values and makes assignment reproducible.
Aligns the covariate’s geographic unit to the official provincial outcome.

coverage.notes: Four provinces lacked a direct 2019 Eurostat NUTS3-density match; three further provinces had zero modeled exceedance days and cannot enter a log-exposure model. All included points had 365 complete modeled exposure days.

effect.scale: OLS log-log coefficient adjusted for log 2019 population density
effect.contrast: 1% higher 2018 CAMS-derived limit-exceedance days at the provincial-capital coordinate

blockers: Exact reproduction of the published 55-city sample is impossible: the article says it was randomly selected but does not identify the cities.
The public national COVID-19 series reports cumulative cases by province, not city.
Four eligible provinces could not be directly matched to 2019 Eurostat NUTS3 density and were not imputed.
Three further provinces had zero CAMS-derived exceedance days; log(0) is undefined, so they were excluded rather than transformed.
